title: The adjunction $K\otimes^{\mathrm L}-\dashv\RHom(K,-)$ on $D_{\mathrm{cons}}$
statement:
Let $X$ and $\Lambda$ be as in [def-sfb-dc-tensor] and [def-sfb-dc-hom]. For
$K\in D_{\mathrm{cons}}(X,\Lambda)$, the adjunction

$$
K\otimes^{\mathrm L}-\dashv\RHom(K,-)\qquad\text{on }D_{\mathrm{cons}}(X,\Lambda)
$$

is the restriction along the fully faithful inclusion of the ambient tensor–hom adjunction for
$K$.

proof.text: Put $\mathcal D=D(\Mod_{\Lambda_X})$ and $\mathcal C=D_{\mathrm{cons}}(X,\Lambda)$. Write $\iota:\mathcal C\hookrightarrow\mathcal D$ for the inclusion. For the fixed $K\in\mathcal C$ let $T_K=(\iota K)\otimes^{\mathrm L}_{\Lambda_X}-$ and $H_K=\RHom_{\Lambda_X}(\iota K,-)$ on $\mathcal D$. The layer-B internal-hom clause of [sk-def-sfb-derived-tensor-hom] gives the ambient adjunction $a:T_K\dashv H_K$, hence natural bijections $a_{A,B}:\Hom_{\mathcal D}(T_K A,B)\simeq\Hom_{\mathcal D}(A,H_K B)$. This uses the relative tensor over $\Lambda_X$, not the tensor of coefficient-valued sheaves in layer A.

source.place: first sentence: the ambient relative tensor–hom adjunction

proof.text: By [def-sfb-dc-tensor] and [def-sfb-dc-hom], the two preservation properties are simultaneous hypotheses on $\Lambda$ in this item. Let $t_K,h_K:\mathcal C\to\mathcal C$ be their specified fixed-$K$ restrictions. Write $H=\RHom_{\Lambda_X}(-,-)$ for the ambient bifunctor. The internal-Hom definition gives $h_K(B)=H(\iota K,\iota B)$ with its bounded-constructibility property, and $h_K(v)=H(1_{\iota K},\iota v)$ on morphisms. Its displayed fixed-$K$ compatibility and the tensor definition give $\iota h_K=H_K\iota$ and $\iota t_K=T_K\iota$ on objects and morphisms. The internal-Hom comparison has identity components, as explicitly stated in [def-sfb-dc-hom]. Thus the endpoints of both Hom identifications in step 3 are the specified ambient objects, with the same maps; $t_KA$ and $h_KB$ belong to $\mathcal C$ for every $A,B\in\mathcal C$. This uses the preservation assumptions themselves and requires no coefficient-specific finiteness theorem.

source.place: second sentence: both functors restrict and commute with inclusion

proof.text: By [sk-def-sfb-bounded-constructible], $\mathcal C$ is a full subcategory with morphisms computed in $\mathcal D$. For $A,B\in\mathcal C$, define $b_{A,B}$ to be the composite $\Hom_{\mathcal C}(t_KA,B)=\Hom_{\mathcal D}(T_K\iota A,\iota B)\xrightarrow{a_{\iota A,\iota B}}\Hom_{\mathcal D}(\iota A,H_K\iota B)=\Hom_{\mathcal C}(A,h_KB)$. Its inverse is the same composite with $a^{-1}$ and the equalities reversed. For $u:A\to A\prime$, $v:B\to B\prime$ and $f:t_KA\prime\to B$, ambient naturality says $b_{A,B\prime}(v\circ f\circ t_Ku)=h_Kv\circ b_{A\prime,B}(f)\circ u$ after inclusion; the inclusions use the same composition, so this is the naturality identity in $\mathcal C$. These mutually inverse natural Hom maps define $t_K\dashv h_K$. Their unit is $b_{A,t_KA}(1_{t_KA})$ and their counit is $b^{-1}_{h_KB,B}(1_{h_KB})$. Under $\iota$, these become $a_{\iota A,T_K\iota A}(1_{T_K\iota A})$ and $a^{-1}_{H_K\iota B,\iota B}(1_{H_K\iota B})$, respectively, which are the ambient unit and counit at the included objects. Thus the adjunction is the specified restriction, with no additional choice of adjunction data.
